input.text: The constant soft hiss of an old VHS camcorder while it records: analog tape noise and the faint steady whir of the tape motor, even and quiet. No voices, no music.
Cold mountain wind blowing outside the closed window of an old stone house: low howling gusts and a faint whistle through the window frame, steady, no rain. No voices, no music.
Night inside an old rented room above a closed bar in a mountain village: deep silence, the wind outside, the old house creaking now and then, a dog barking far away. No voices, no music.
The steady electric hum of an old refrigerator in a small kitchen, recorded close, with the faint buzz of a fluorescent tube light. No voices, no music.
An old wall clock ticking slowly and clearly in a silent living room, with a low cold draft in the background. No voices, no music.
The slow, heavy, wheezing breath of a very sick woman lying in bed in a dark room, recorded close, steady and rhythmic. No voices, no music.

The steady mechanical buzz of an old electric nebulizer compressor running in a small bare room, with the soft bubbling hiss of the medicine mist and, now and then, a slow wheezing breath through the mask. No voices, no music.
A single footstep of a heavy boot on old creaky wooden floorboards, close and dry. No voices, no music.
One heavy boot step on an old wooden plank floor, with a faint creak, close and dry. No voices, no music.
A single slow footstep on worn wooden floorboards indoors, a dull thud, close and dry. No voices, no music.
An old thermal fax machine receiving a page: a short modem handshake screech, then the clicking whir of the printer slowly feeding out paper. No voices, no music.
A sheet of paper picked up from a wooden desk: a quick, crisp rustle. No voices, no music.
A folded newspaper being opened: crisp rustling of large paper pages. No voices, no music.
A rubber stamp pressed hard onto paper on a wooden desk: a single dull thud. No voices, no music.
A ballpoint pen quickly signing a name on paper on a desk: short scratchy strokes. No voices, no music.
An old wooden door slowly creaking open in a silent dark house. No voices, no music.
The tiny electric zoom motor of a 1990s camcorder whirring as it zooms in. No voices, no music.
The short electronic double beep of a 1990s camcorder starting to record. No voices, no music.
A VHS cassette pushed into an old video recorder: the mechanism clunks, whirs, and the tape starts playing. No voices, no music.
An old wooden chair creaking under someone sitting down at a desk. No voices, no music.
A sharp VHS tape glitch: a short burst of static and a warped, distorted low electronic stab. No voices, no music.
A deep, slow, unsettling gust of wind in a dark room that sounds almost like a long whispered breath, rising and fading. No voices, no music.
A few coins dropped and clinking on a wooden desk. No voices, no music.
A short crackle of analog VHS tape static, like a glitch in an old videotape playback. No voices, no music.
The click of an old bakelite lamp switch being turned off on a desk. No voices, no music.
